subject: ashPhoenix
kind: god body portrait (plan 3.1: whole body, regal pose, variant 0, swatch 0)
prompt:
Image 1 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing: this painting shows a whole figure from head to foot. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 1.

A full-length painted portrait of the Ash Phoenix, an undying firebird-god of ash and ember that rises again after death, in a regal pose: perched upright on the ground, its head raised high, its chest out, its great wings spread half open and raised behind it like fans, its long tail sweeping down to the ground and curling forward. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the plume crest about 6% from the top edge and the tail and talons about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the crest, the head and the wings that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the tail and talons.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the plume crest, the fan-spread wings and the long tail against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the bird is its long flight feathers: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows: there is no flame, no fire and no glow, only a faint trail of dull ember specks. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Body: a great bird of prey shaped like an eagle with a long neck; its body feathers are coal-dark, charred black-brown (#3A2A24), each barred with thin pale ash-grey bars; a hooked beak of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn; dark eyes; strong taloned feet of dark grey. Crest: a tall plume crest of long feathers sweeping back from its brow. Wings: broad, rounded wings spread like fans, the long flight feathers dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour, barred with darker bands. Tail: a long tail of trailing feathers. A faint trail of dull ember specks drifts from the wing tips and the tail.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view.
variant0: variant 0 of every slot: plume crest; fan plumage (wings); long tail; barred feathers; flame trail
